title: Every commit has an ID
concept: git log --oneline, hashes and git show

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: As the festival grows, our history gets longer.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Try `git log --oneline` to see a quick list.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: See those short codes at the start? They are commit IDs (or hashes).

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: You can look closely at any past commit by typing `git show` and its ID.

items.text: Find out what changed in the middle commit

questions.prompt: Run `git log --oneline`. What does every line start with?

choices.text: A short mix of numbers and letters (the commit ID or hash)

questions.explanation: That short code is the commit ID or hash. It's how git names your save points.

questions.prompt: Run `git log --oneline` to find the ID for "Add menu". Then run `git show <that-id>`. Which file was added?
questions.explanation: `git show` tells you exactly what a specific commit did.

hints: Run `git log --oneline` to answer the first question.
Look for the commit message 'Add menu' in the log, take its ID, and run `git show <ID>`.
recap: `git log --oneline` shows a summary. `git show <commit-ID>` shows the exact changes in that save point.

cheatSheet.summary: View history as a short list with commit IDs
View the exact changes in a specific commit
